Subject: Logs retention baseline for integration pilot

Hi Rachel / Marissa,

As we prepare for the integration pilot next month, our security team has a couple of clarifying questions about Redwood's default log retention. Specifically:

- What is the default retention window for raw request payloads (the exact user input) versus the model responses?
- Are partial/streamed token fragments stored anywhere, or are they ephemeral until the final output is assembled?
- Do you classify prompts (user-provided text) as data that is retained by default, or are prompts marked transient unless explicitly opted in?
- What artifacts/evidence can Redwood provide to prove deletion (e.g., audit logs, proof-of-deletion reports) for a customer-requested purge?

We need concise answers (bulleted) that we can share with our compliance gate. If you have a short summary doc or a CSV of default retention tables, please attach.

Thanks,

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear list. Short answers below, and I attached a compact summary (retention-summary.pdf) plus a CSV that shows our default windows by artifact type. Happy to expand any point.

- Default windows (hosted API, US region):
  • Raw request input (user prompt): retained 30 days by default; can be reduced via customer-level settings or retention flags.
  • Final model response (finalized output): retained 90 days by default for debugging/quality analytics; customers may request shorter retention or opt for non-persistent responses.
  • Streaming fragments / interim tokens: not persisted to long-term store by default; the serving runtime buffers fragments transiently in memory and they are not written to persistent logs unless the request is configured for debug-level capture.
  • Derivative artifacts (embeddings, indexes, logs exported to S3): retention depends on the export destination; exported artifacts follow the destination's lifecycle unless you use Redwood-managed exports.

- Prompts vs inputs: we treat the term "prompt" as synonymous with the raw request payload. By default they are retained (30d) for support + quality, but customers can set the request to be ephemeral and we will bypass persistent write paths.

- Proof of deletion: we provide (a) deletion audit logs with timestamps and job IDs, (b) a proof-of-deletion artifact on request (signed job record), and (c) optional third-party attestation for enterprise contracts.

I've looped in Kimberley and Marissa for procurement / policy language. If you want a one-page statement for your compliance packet we can produce that as well.

Best,
Rachel Kim

Hi Alicia — Karthik from the infra team here, adding the granular technical detail Rachel mentioned and a suggested SOW paragraph below.

- What is retained: the default 30d window for request payloads includes the original user text and structured metadata necessary for routing (request id, region shard id). We do NOT retain low-level network headers beyond what is needed for tracing (trace id) and those are redacted from long-term stores.

- Streaming fragments: streaming buffers are ephemeral in the serving runtime only. They are never flushed to persistent blob storage unless the customer has enabled "debug capture" for specific sessions.

- Deletion SLA & evidence:
  • Standard SLA: deletion job queued and completed within 48 hours for hosted customers (subject to backlog).
  • For enterprise contracts, we offer an accelerated 24-hour deletion SLA as an add-on.
  • Proof: after the deletion job runs we emit a signed deletion_report JSON with the job id, scope (record ids/time range), and ledger entry; a human-readable PDF proof can be generated on request.

Suggested SOW paragraph (plain-language):
"Redwood Inference retains customer request payloads (user-provided prompts) for a default period of 30 days and final model responses for 90 days in the hosted service to support diagnostics and quality monitoring. Customers may elect ephemeral mode to prevent persistent storage of request payloads. Upon a customer-initiated deletion request Redwood will run a verifiable purge and provide a signed deletion report within the agreed SLA (standard 48 hours; enterprise 24 hours)."

If you want, we can tighten the default windows for this pilot (e.g., set prompt retention to 7 days) and produce the SOW paragraph with those numbers.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
